task.name: A dispatch refused because the account may not call the model quarantines that model for the rest of the run
task.story_text:
---
depends_on:
  - issue-2950
---

## What

Slice 3 of 3 from the decomposition of #2914. When a dispatch is refused for a reason that is a property of the configuration rather than the request — the account may not call this model — that model is quarantined for the remainder of the run: no later story, phase or role routes to it, and the run continues on the remaining models. The initial availability classification (#2949) and the pre-dispatch empty-pool stop (#2950) are the earlier slices; this one covers what the router learns *from* a refusal it did not predict.

## Why

Availability resolution cannot be perfect: a provider may publish no catalog (unverified), the catalog may lag the provider's actual policy, or the answer may go stale mid-sprint. An explicit refusal is stronger evidence than any prior state. Without quarantine, a sprint meets the identical refusal once per story, paying WORKSPACE, preflight, routing and plan each time — which is exactly what happened across four stories on 2026-09-04. The existing transient-failure quarantine in `provider_health` is adjacent (reviewer-only, time-windowed, pattern-matched on capacity and rate-limit strings) and does not cover configuration refusals or all phases and roles. See #2914.

## Acceptance criteria

- A dispatch refused because the account may not call the selected model is classified as a configuration refusal, distinct from a request-level or transient failure. The classification does not depend on matching one provider's message text: a refusal the classifier cannot attribute is treated as transient and retried within the existing bounded retry budget, never quarantined and never retried unboundedly.
- A configuration refusal quarantines that model for the remainder of the run. No later story, phase or role in that run routes to it, and every exclusion it causes is recorded in the routing decision with a reason naming the refusal that triggered it.
- Quarantine applies to an unverified model as much as to one the availability answer called available: the refusal converts unverified to unavailable for the rest of that run.
- A configuration refusal is a routing outcome, not an agent failure: it is never recorded against the model's capability history and never counts as a dev or review failure for the story.
- The story whose dispatch was refused continues on the remaining models where any remain, and stops before further spend, naming the excluded models, where none do — the same outcome #2950 defines for an empty pool.
- Quarantine is scoped to the run. The next run resolves availability afresh (#2949) rather than inheriting a quarantine that may no longer hold.

## Example

```
  ▸ DEV   gpt-5.4  iter=1
  ✗ DEV   refused — account may not call openai/gpt-5.4/cli under codex
          ChatGPT-account auth (HTTP 400). Quarantined for the rest of run 68aec168166d.
  ▸ DEV   gpt-5.6-terra  iter=1
  ✓ DEV   $0.51  5m 02s

  ... later story, same run ...
  ⚠ ROUTING  openai/gpt-5.4/cli excluded — quarantined after configuration refusal on issue-2775
```

Consequently an OpenAI tool-loop configuration refusal can escape as an exception instead of reaching Step 5's routing helper, while an unattributed 400 cannot enter the required bounded retry path. The proposed tool-loop tests only assert that the record is written and the 400 remains re-raised, so they preserve rather than detect this broken outcome path.

Convert configuration and unattributed refusals into _failure_result results carrying their stable codes, or explicitly add an outer exception-to-AgentResult seam and test end-to-end DEV/review rerouting plus bounded retry for an unattributed tool-loop 400.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 1 calls src/theforge/model_quarantine.py an import leaf with no theforge imports while requiring it to import DispatchIdentity, make_identity, and identity_of from theforge.runners.rate_registry.   Suggestion: Keep the decision as planned; if the runbook paragraph is trimmed during implementation, keep the sentence telling an operator reading a merge failure to look for the routing-stop wording, since that is the whole mitigation.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 2 says to also record at 'the api.py:437/:471/:510/:734 _failure_result sites only where a provider exception is in scope', but :510 is the stuck-detection terminate — no provider exception is in scope there, and _call_with_retry's terminal exit is reached only after the retry loop has already exhausted its budget, so the identity may have been dispatched several times before the record lands.

When comparing injected knowledge with review findings, authorship and exposure provenance must be recorded at claim level, because a reviewer can repeat a claim from their own prompt and that must not be attributed as missed uptake by development.

A finding's grounding status needs to be recomputed each review cycle from current story evidence, because a previously ungrounded P1 can later become grounded and should then participate in blocking decisions.
Non-blocking dispositions for ungrounded findings must be honored consistently by escalation and topology analysis, not just by the immediate review verdict path.

The current AgentResult exposes only the generic provider_refused_before_generation code.

Step 4 does not actually cover all in-run dispatch sites. preflight_decomposition_flow.generate_decomposition_assessment() and escalation_advisor_flow.run_escalation_advisor() invoke run_agent and hide the AgentResult behind higher-level return values; workspace._resolve_merge_conflicts() also dispatches a model during landing. This directly breaks the all-phases/roles and later-story guarantees.

Step 1 only normalizes Codex CLI refusals. The API path in runners/api.py re-raises HTTP 400 from AgentLoopManager.run(), and _run_loop_openai() only converts tool-related 400s, so an account/model refusal over API bypasses AgentResult and the classifier entirely. Other runner paths likewise receive no proposed structured refusal contract.

Step 3 names _run_one_story(), which does not exist; the sprint worker is _run_single_story() in src/theforge/sprint/runner.py. Step 6 names nonexistent src/theforge/audit.py and src/theforge/audit_render.py; the real files are src/theforge/coordinator/audit.py and src/theforge/coordinator/audit_render.py.

Step 1's attribution basis does not exist in the data. The only structured refusal evidence codex emits is HTTP status 400 plus error.type == invalid_request_error (runner_codex.py:476-521, PRE_GENERATION_REFUSAL_CODE at :483), and the verbatim payload for this exact incident — captured in tests/fake_bin/npx:217-233 and tests/test_runner_codex.py:391-394 — carries only {status, type, message}. There is no account/model-access field to key on, and 400/invalid_request_error is shared with ordinary request-level 400s (bad param, oversized context). So 'classify account-not-allowed-for-model from stable structured refusal fields and leave generic provider_refused_before_generation unattributed' resolves the story's own example refusal ('The gpt-5.4 model is not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account') to unattributed → transient retry → never quarantined. The plan's Risk 1 mitigation ('only quarantine when the runner provides structured account/model-access evidence') concedes rather than retires this: it leaves the story's primary acceptance criterion and its worked example unimplemented while every test in Step 7 could still pass against synthetic events with fields the provider does not send.
Step 6 lists src/theforge/audit.py and src/theforge/audit_render.py; neither path exists. The modules are src/theforge/coordinator/audit.py and src/theforge/coordinator/audit_render.py.

Step 3 names sprint runner entry points that do not exist: there is no _run_one_story() in src/theforge/sprint/runner.py (the per-story entries are _run_single_story() at :2240 and _run_inherited_story() at :2731), and _run_fresh() lives in sprint/runner.py:2107, not in engine.py as the step's grouping implies.

Classification is added only in runner_codex.py (Step 1), so an identical configuration refusal from the claude or gemini runner produces no quarantine. The acceptance criteria are written over 'a dispatch', not over codex specifically.

Step 1 claims runner-wide API normalization but lists only runners/api.py. Single-shot calls are handled by runners/adapters/openai.py::_run_openai_chat/_run_openai_responses, adapters/anthropic.py::_run_anthropic, and adapters/google.py::_run_google; each catches the provider exception and returns AgentResult with raw={} and only a formatted output string. By the time runners/api.py receives that result, HTTP status and provider error type/code—the structured gate required by the plan—have been discarded. Tool-free API dispatches therefore cannot reliably classify or quarantine a configuration refusal.

Step 2's StoryAvailability overlay cannot enforce quarantine for model-preference or transport fallbacks. StoryAvailability.for_profile() and by_agent() consult only profile_dispatch_key(profile, config), which represents the primary dispatch. run_api_agent() and runners/cli.py::_maybe_run_api_fallback() choose fallback_models internally. A refused fallback identity remains invisible to later routing, while quarantining a primary excludes the entire profile even when one of its fallback models remains usable.

Step 3 says to scope by the sprint run id and pass the existing sprint_run_id argument, but sprint/runner.py generates SprintExecutionState.sprint_run_id anew on every process generation. Repository semantics explicitly treat a mid-sprint re-exec as a new generation of the same run, and _run_inherited_story() is reached after that boundary. Keying the ledger by this regenerated id starts an empty quarantine precisely when an inherited or later story must retain it.

Step 4's new landing status value has consumers beyond the three land_story callers it enumerates. land_story's status is persisted and queried downstream: audit_storage.py:1635-1641 defaults a missing landing_status to 'landed' and writes it to the landing_status TEXT column (:316, :3026-3052), audit_read_model.py:326/583 selects it, and issue_cost.py:96 reads it off the record. plan_structured.approach: Model quarantine as an INSTALLED run-scoped registry, not threaded state — the pattern runners/rate_registry.py already establishes for dispatch rates. Nothing carries a refusal object. Each concrete dispatch attempt classifies its own provider exception at the seam where the structured facts still exist, WRITES a configuration refusal into the installed ledger, and stamps a stable failure_code on the AgentResult it returns so the classifier outcome survives the loss of the exception. Two consumers read the ledger by exact dispatch identity: model_availability resolution, which every router already calls, and runners/cli.py::run_agent, which refuses a quarantined identity before spending. Signature changes are confined to two places where the code cannot work without them: an out-parameter on _resolve_merge_conflicts (copying the selection_out pattern already in that function) and a resolver-profile selection there. _select_advisor_profile, land_story, _merge_branch's contract, CoordinatorState, engine and the sprint runner are untouched.

steps.description: Create the installed run-scoped quarantine ledger, provider-neutral refusal facts, and the three-outcome classifier with stable failure codes.
steps.details:
Model the module on src/theforge/runners/rate_registry.py and REUSE its identity: import DispatchIdentity / make_identity / identity_of rather than re-deriving the canonical (provider, model, transport) triple. QuarantineKey = frozen (identity, base_url). Take the profile-shaped input through a QuarantinableProfile(Protocol) that extends rate_registry's PricedProfile shape with base_url, so the module stays an import leaf (no theforge imports) and can be read from adapters, runners, model_availability, workspace and audit without a cycle. Docstring must state WHY quarantine keys on base_url where pricing does not: a rate is a property of the model, but an entitlement is a property of the credential and endpoint that was refused — two base_urls on one model are two entitlements, and quarantining both from one refusal would take a usable model away from the operator. key_of() returns None on any missing component rather than inserting a partial key.

QuarantineRecord: key, normalized refusal message, provider status and error code, phase, story ref, run id, timestamp. Module-level install()/current()/reset()/contextmanager scope with a threading.Lock (sprint workers write concurrently), mirroring rate_registry's install/active/reset/scoped_registry.

PROVIDER-NEUTRAL CLASSIFICATION, in two layers — this is the fix for the carried Risk 2. Layer one is per-provider structured NORMALIZATION into a provider-neutral RefusalFacts (http status, neutral error category, provider's own code string, normalized message, attempt identity). Each provider contributes its own vocabulary:
  - openai/codex: status 400 with error.type invalid_request_error (the shape at runner_codex.py:502-521, and the one observed real incident), plus 403 with permission/insufficient-quota-style codes.
  - anthropic: permission_error and authentication_error types, and 403.
  - google: 403 PERMISSION_DENIED and the 404 model-not-available-to-caller shape.
  - anything else: category UNKNOWN.
Layer two is ONE provider-agnostic rule over RefusalFacts: CONFIGURATION_REFUSAL requires a normalized category of ENTITLEMENT-or-PRE_GENERATION_REJECT **and** message evidence that names the attempted model/dispatch identity and carries account / plan / auth-mode / entitlement / access / not-allowed / unsupported-for-account meaning. The two-signal rule is preserved but is no longer spelled in one provider's envelope vocabulary. Category UNKNOWN, or a known category without the message evidence, is UNATTRIBUTED_REFUSAL. Facts attributable to the request itself (bad parameter, context length, unsupported tool schema) are REQUEST_REFUSAL.

THE DATA PATH FOR THE TRANSIENT SPLIT — the classifier outcome must survive the death of the provider exception, so each outcome has a stable failure_code that refusal sites stamp on the returned AgentResult:
  - provider_refusal_unattributed  → bounded transient retry
  - provider_refusal_request       → ordinary failure (today's behaviour)
  - provider_refusal_configuration → routing outcome, never retried, ledger already written
  - model_quarantined              → the pre-dispatch backstop result (Step 2), which never reached a provider and must never be re-classified from prose
Export these as module constants plus a is_routing_outcome_code() / is_bounded_retry_code() pair, so dev_phase and review_pool key on the code, not on message text. Note in the docstring that provider_refused_before_generation, the existing code, is retained for compatibility but is no longer the discriminator — it was one code carrying two meanings, which is the defect.

steps.description: Record refusals at every concrete dispatch seam — including the shared tool-loop seam — and skip quarantined identities inside the internal fallback loops.
steps.details:
The record is written by the refused attempt, so a later fallback succeeding cannot erase it and no AgentResult has to carry the evidence object.

THE SHARED TOOL-LOOP SEAM (the missed path). AgentLoopManager.run's `except Exception` at api.py:376-380 is where tool-bearing dispatches lose their provider exception: status_code == 400 is RE-RAISED for _run_loop_openai's tool-not-supported fallback, and everything else is flattened into _failure_result(f"Provider API error: {exc}"). Normalize and classify INSIDE that except block, before either branch — record a CONFIGURATION_REFUSAL into the ledger and stamp the outcome code, then preserve today's control flow exactly (still re-raise 400, still flatten otherwise) so the tool-not-supported fallback is unaffected. Do the same at _call_with_retry's own terminal-failure exit and at the api.py:437/:471/:510/:734 _failure_result sites only where a provider exception is in scope. Give _failure_result a failure_code_override pass-through for the stamp — it already takes that argument (api.py:510 uses it for stuck_pattern), so this is not a new mechanism. DEV and review refusals on the normal tool loop are quarantined by this hook, not by the single-shot hooks.

SINGLE-SHOT ADAPTERS. _run_openai_chat, _run_openai_responses, _run_anthropic and _run_google each catch the provider exception and flatten it to raw={} plus a formatted string. Normalize/classify/record INSIDE that except block while status and error type still exist, and stamp the code on the returned AgentResult. runners/api.py then re-derives nothing from prose.

Both seams call the SAME per-provider normalizer from Step 1, so a provider's vocabulary is stated once and both the tool-bearing and tool-free paths get it.

CODEX. _classify_pre_generation_refusal() (runner_codex.py:525) already isolates the message behind the structured gate; build RefusalFacts from the same event, record, and stamp. runner_claude / runner_gemini: record at the point they observe a provider refusal, or add a comment naming the fact that no such structured observation point exists yet — not a TODO, a statement of the current seam.

FALLBACK LOOPS. run_api_agent()'s fallback_models loop and cli.py::_maybe_run_api_fallback() consult current() and SKIP an already-quarantined exact identity rather than dispatching it. Each attempt they do make records under its own identity, so a refused fallback is visible to later routing.

PRE-DISPATCH BACKSTOP. run_agent() gets a quarantine check mirroring the capability_transport_refusal / _capability_refusal_result pair already at cli.py:645-648 and :700: a quarantined identity returns a zero-cost failure AgentResult carrying the quarantine reason AND failure_code model_quarantined, before any transport is invoked. The distinct code matters — this result never went to a provider, so nothing downstream may re-classify it from its message text.

steps.description: Read the ledger inside availability resolution, and re-overlay at each phase boundary so an intra-story refusal is not masked by a stale answer.
steps.details:
model_availability.py's docstring establishes that it supplies the fact while assignment.py owns exclusion policy, and the runbook records that the answer is read per story. Overlay quarantine where the fact is produced — inside resolve_story_availability (:356) and resolve_agent_availability (:388) — turning a quarantined identity's answer into unavailable with a detail naming the triggering refusal, phase and story. Every downstream consumer (by_agent, for_profile, phase_candidate_sets, unavailable_candidates, preflight's per-phase pass, the #2950 empty-pool stop, static-routing and pinned-pool paths) inherits quarantine with zero signature changes.

INTRA-STORY STALENESS. Resolution is per story but a refusal is learned mid-story, so a phase holding a StoryAvailability resolved BEFORE the refusal keeps the stale answer. Two mechanisms, stated explicitly rather than assumed: (a) add a cheap requarantine overlay — StoryAvailability.with_current_quarantine(), pure and allocation-light — and apply it at each phase boundary within the story where the coordinator already re-reads availability, so a later phase in the SAME story sees the refusal; (b) the run_agent backstop of Step 2 is the guaranteed floor for any holder we did not re-overlay: it cannot spend, worst case it returns model_quarantined and Step 5's helper reroutes. Say (b) is a deliberate backstop, not an oversight.

Add format_quarantined_detail() beside format_unavailable_detail / format_unverified_detail so a runtime quarantine is distinguishable from static catalog unavailability. Unverified is overridden to unavailable only for an exact quarantined key, satisfying the unverified-conversion criterion while leaving every other unverified model eligible.

NOT threaded, and why each is safe: for_profile()/by_agent() key on profile_dispatch_key(profile, config) — the primary — but a quarantined fallback is now unreachable via Step 2's loop skip plus the pre-dispatch refusal, so profile-level granularity cannot under-enforce; and a profile whose primary is quarantined but whose configured fallback is not is handled by the #2950 reseat the runbook documents, so it is not over-excluded.

steps.description: Install the ledger for a run and rehydrate it across a re-exec generation, gated on the captured reexec signal rather than the popped env marker.
steps.details:
Do NOT key on SprintExecutionState.sprint_run_id: runner.py:5536 regenerates it every process generation, so an inherited story would start empty exactly where it must retain the quarantine. Persist and rehydrate under sprint_id, the identity that survives.

Do NOT gate rehydration on _previous_run_marker_present() either — that was wrong for a concrete reason. cli/sprint.py:200-208 captures `reexec = _is_reexec()` BEFORE detach.setup_detached_child() pops FORGE_PREV_RUN_ID (detach.py:491), and :307-308 carries an explicit comment not to recompute it because the env signal is gone. Ledger installation inside run_sprint would therefore see the marker absent on the normal detached re-exec path and start empty, losing quarantine mid-run. Gate restoration on SprintRunContext.reexec — the captured, authoritative signal that is already threaded to run_sprint (cli/sprint.py:289, :409; runner.py:3670, :5664) — so no new plumbing is required.

PERSIST SYNCHRONOUSLY, BEFORE re-exec. A record written at refusal time must already be on disk when the process is replaced, so write each QuarantineRecord through to the progressive run-state surface (sprint-audit.yaml under the same sprint_id, beside where _read_prior_sprint_cost at runner.py:683-691 already reads carry-forward) at the moment it is recorded, not at run teardown. Teardown is not guaranteed to run before an execv.

Install the scope once at sprint launch (beside where sprint_run_id and the structured logger are set up) and once in coordinator engine for standalone forge run, keyed there by story run id. Records live only in current-run state and audit — a new sprint invocation, with reexec False, resolves #2949 availability afresh.

steps.description: Reroute the refused phase onto remaining models, split the transient bucket by failure code, and make the landing conflict-resolver quarantine-aware.
steps.details:
First run `rg -n 'run_agent\(|run_agent_pool\(' src/theforge/` (definitions at runners/cli.py:608 and :794) and record the full output plus a one-line per-site disposition — rerouted, or deliberately outside run-scoped story execution and why — in the story's implementation notes AND as a comment on the shared helper, so a later reader can tell a deliberate exclusion from an overlooked one.

SHARED REROUTE HELPER. After a dispatch, ask whether the attempt just made became quarantined (ledger record, or failure_code model_quarantined / provider_refusal_configuration); on yes, re-resolve availability for the current phase — which now excludes it via Step 3 — and retry on what remains; when nothing remains, return the existing NoAvailableModelError / routing_stop_message outcome #2950 defines. The helper takes no scope argument (it reads current()), so wrapping a site is a one-line change. Apply at the phase dispatch sites above including the wrappers that hide AgentResult (generate_decomposition_assessment, run_escalation_advisor). Before rerouting, ensure a configuration refusal is never recorded against capability history, provider_health, dev/review failure counts or reviewer verdicts.

TRANSIENT SPLIT, keyed on Step 1's codes rather than the raw provider_refused_before_generation code, so one code cannot land in two buckets. _is_transient_dev_failure (dev_phase.py:330-350) and review_pool's checks (:78-80, :180, :221) both fall through to output-prose matching today, which would misread the backstop result. Have both consult is_bounded_retry_code() / is_routing_outcome_code() BEFORE the prose fallthrough: provider_refusal_unattributed consumes the configured bounded transport retry budget; provider_refusal_request keeps today's ordinary-failure behaviour; provider_refusal_configuration and model_quarantined are routing outcomes that never enter the retry path — otherwise a phase burns its budget re-dispatching an identity refused every time.

THE LANDING PATH IS IN SCOPE — my previous plan's Risk-3 mitigation was factually wrong and is withdrawn. _resolve_merge_conflicts (workspace.py:283) receives run_agent's AgentResult but at :350 discards result.output and returns False, and _merge_branch at :607 then reports the ORIGINAL git merge error — so the backstop's routing-stop text could never surface. It also always uses config.dev_profile (:342) with no way to pick a remaining model, so landing would fail even when another eligible model exists.   - Add `routing_out: list[str] | None = None`, a keyword defaulting to None so no existing caller or test breaks. Because the bool return, _merge_branch's info dict shape, land_story()'s (merge_info, landing_status) tuple and all three of its callers are unchanged, tests/test_validation_profiles.py and every other caller of the bool are unaffected — and no routing exception can escape on the sprint scheduler thread, because none is raised.

plan.approach: Model quarantine as an INSTALLED run-scoped registry, not threaded state — the exact pattern runners/rate_registry.py already establishes for dispatch rates. Nothing carries a refusal. Each concrete dispatch attempt WRITES its own refusal into the installed ledger at the moment it is refused (including attempts inside the internal fallback loops), and the two consumers READ it by exact dispatch identity: model_availability resolution, which every router already calls per story, and runners/cli.py::run_agent, which refuses a quarantined identity before spending. Because the ledger is installed rather than passed, no signature changes are needed in _select_advisor_profile, land_story, _merge_branch, _resolve_merge_conflicts, CoordinatorState, engine or the sprint runner — the landing path is covered by the pre-dispatch refusal plus the existing #2950 empty-pool text, with no change to its boolean contract.

steps.description: Create the installed run-scoped quarantine ledger and the three-outcome refusal classifier.
steps.details:
Model the module directly on src/theforge/runners/rate_registry.py: a frozen QuarantineKey reusing the same canonical (provider, model, transport) triple plus base_url so two credentials/endpoints on one model stay two identities (the runbook's 'a candidate is a dispatch identity, not a model name'); a make_key()/key_of(profile) pair that returns None on any missing component rather than inserting a partial key; a QuarantineRecord (key, refusal message, provider status/error type, phase, story ref, run id, timestamp); and module-level install()/current()/contextmanager scope with a threading.Lock, since sprint workers write concurrently. Keep it an import leaf like rate_registry (no theforge imports) so it can be read from adapters, runners, model_availability and audit without a cycle.

The classifier returns one of three outcomes, never a bool: CONFIGURATION_REFUSAL (quarantine), UNATTRIBUTED_REFUSAL (bounded transient retry), REQUEST_REFUSAL (ordinary invocation failure). Input is a small structured RefusalObservation (http status, provider error type/code, normalized message, the concrete attempt identity) — built by callers at the point they still hold the provider's exception or event, never re-derived from prose. CONFIGURATION_REFUSAL requires BOTH the structured pre-generation gate (mirroring the existing two-signal rule at runner_codex.py:502-521 — status 400 AND invalid_request_error, because either alone is weaker than the claim) AND provider-agnostic message evidence: the message names the attempted model/dispatch identity and carries account / plan / auth-mode / entitlement / access / not-allowed / unsupported-for-account evidence. Anything matching the structured gate but not the message rule is UNATTRIBUTED_REFUSAL. Anything attributable to the request itself (bad parameter, context length) is REQUEST_REFUSAL. Docstring states the contract is runner-wide and that Codex currently emits the one observed real incident shape.

steps.description: Record refusals at each concrete attempt, in the runners and adapters, and skip quarantined identities inside the internal fallback loops.
steps.details:
This step is what makes the recurring fallback-evidence P1 structurally impossible: the record is written by the refused attempt, so a later fallback succeeding cannot erase it and no AgentResult has to carry it.

Codex: _classify_pre_generation_refusal() (runner_codex.py:525) already isolates the refusal message behind the structured gate; build a RefusalObservation there from the same event and record CONFIGURATION_REFUSAL into the installed ledger before returning. API adapters: _run_openai_chat / _run_openai_responses / _run_anthropic / _run_google each catch the provider exception and flatten it to raw={} plus a formatted string — build and classify the RefusalObservation INSIDE that except block, while status and error.type still exist, and record there. This is the fix for the prior P1-impl about single-shot dispatches; runners/api.py then needs no re-derivation from prose. runner_claude / runner_gemini: record at the equivalent point where they observe a provider refusal, or leave a named TODO-free comment stating no such observation point exists yet.

Internal fallback loops: run_api_agent()'s fallback_models loop and cli.py::_maybe_run_api_fallback() consult current() and SKIP an already-quarantined exact identity rather than dispatching it. Each attempt they do make records its own refusal under its own identity, so a refused fallback is visible to later routing — the dominant recurring theme.

run_agent(): add a pre-dispatch quarantine check that mirrors the existing capability_transport_refusal / _capability_refusal_result pair already at cli.py:648 and :700 — a quarantined identity returns a zero-cost failure AgentResult carrying the quarantine reason, before any transport is invoked. This is the backstop that guarantees no caller anywhere can spend on a quarantined model, whether or not it consulted availability.

steps.description: Read the ledger inside availability resolution so every existing router excludes quarantined identities with no signature change.
steps.details:
model_availability.py's own docstring establishes that it 'supplies the fact and its presentation' while assignment.py owns the exclusion policy, and the runbook records that 'the answer is read per story, not once at launch.' So overlay quarantine where the fact is produced — inside resolve_story_availability / resolve_agent_availability — turning a quarantined identity's answer into unavailable with a detail naming the triggering refusal, phase and story. Every downstream consumer (by_agent, for_profile, phase_candidate_sets, unavailable_candidates, preflight's per-phase pass, the empty-pool stop, the static-routing and pinned-pool paths) then inherits quarantine with zero changes: _select_advisor_profile, land_story, engine and the sprint runner are untouched because none of them are asked to carry the state.

Specifically NOT threaded, and here is why each is safe: for_profile()/by_agent() key on profile_dispatch_key(profile, config) — the primary — but a quarantined fallback is now unreachable by Step 2's loop skip and its pre-dispatch refusal, so profile-level granularity no longer under-enforces; and a profile whose primary is quarantined but whose configured fallback is not is already handled by the #2950 reseat the runbook documents ('an unavailable primary with an available configured fallback reseats onto the fallback and says so'), so it is not over-excluded. Add format_quarantined_detail() beside the existing format_unavailable_detail/format_unverified_detail so the reason is distinguishable from static catalog unavailability. Unverified is overridden to unavailable only for an exact quarantined key, satisfying the unverified-conversion criterion while leaving every other unverified model fully eligible.

steps.description: Install the ledger for a run, and rehydrate it across a re-exec generation using the mechanism that already carries sprint cost.
steps.details: Do NOT key on SprintExecutionState.sprint_run_id: runner.py:5536 regenerates it on every process generation, so an inherited story would start empty exactly where it must retain the quarantine. Instead reuse the mechanism the same file already uses for exactly this problem — _read_prior_sprint_cost(project_root, sprint_id) at runner.py:683 reads carry-forward from sprint-audit.yaml gated on _previous_run_marker_present(). Persist quarantine records to the same sprint-audit.yaml under the same sprint_id and rehydrate them on install under the same previous-run-marker gate, so a mid-run re-exec inherits them and a fresh sprint invocation does not. Install the scope once at sprint launch (beside where sprint_run_id and the structured logger are set up) and once in the coordinator engine for standalone forge run, keyed there by story run id. Records live only in current-run state and audit — a new run resolves #2949 availability afresh.

steps.description: Reroute the refused phase onto remaining models, and split the transient bucket by classifier outcome.
steps.details:
First run `rg -n 'run_agent\(|run_agent_pool\(' src/theforge/` (the definitions are runners/cli.py:608 and :794) and record the full output plus a one-line per-site disposition — rerouted, or deliberately outside run-scoped story execution and why — in the story's implementation notes AND as a comment on the shared helper, so a later reader can tell a deliberate exclusion from an overlooked one.

Add one small shared helper that, after a dispatch, asks the ledger whether the attempt it just made became quarantined; on yes it re-resolves availability for the current phase (which now excludes it, via Step 3) and retries on what remains, and when nothing remains returns the existing NoAvailableModelError / routing_stop_message outcome #2950 already defines. Crucially the helper takes no scope argument — it reads current() — so wrapping a site is a one-line change, not a signature change. Apply it at the phase dispatch sites above, including the wrappers that hide AgentResult (generate_decomposition_assessment, run_escalation_advisor). Before that reroute, ensure a configuration refusal is never recorded against capability history, provider_health, dev/review failure counts or reviewer verdicts — it is a routing outcome.

Transient split: have the transient checks consult the Step 1 classifier outcome, not the raw failure_code, so one provider_refused_before_generation code cannot land in two buckets. Today that code is in no transient set (dev_phase.py:344 lists only rate_limit / provider_internal_error / connection_reset, and config.retry.review_transient_failure_codes matches), so refusals fail the phase outright. Change ONLY UNATTRIBUTED_REFUSAL to consume the configured bounded transport retry budget; REQUEST_REFUSAL keeps today's ordinary-failure behaviour; CONFIGURATION_REFUSAL never enters the retry path.

The landing path is deliberately NOT in this list and needs no change. workspace._resolve_merge_conflicts() (workspace.py:283) dispatches through run_agent, so Step 2's pre-dispatch refusal already prevents spend on a quarantined model and Step 3 already prevents its selection; where nothing remains, the failure text it returns through _merge_branch carries the #2950 routing-stop wording naming the excluded models. Its bool contract, _merge_branch's info['error'], land_story()'s (merge_info, landing_status) tuple and all three of its callers are untouched, so no routing exception can escape on the sprint scheduler thread — there is none to escape.

steps.description: Surface quarantine in routing decisions and audit, and cover the seams with tests.
steps.details:
Every later candidate_pool entry excluded by quarantine carries format_quarantined_detail() naming the refusal that triggered it, rendered in coordinator and sprint audit and distinguishable from static model_unavailable. Extend the runbook's 'Model availability gate' section (docs/guides/controller-runbook.md:92) with the runtime-quarantine paragraph and the spec's example lines — the runbook is where forge's availability behaviour is stated, so leaving it unstated is how the next reader infers the wrong call path.

Tests: the three classifier outcomes using the verbatim tests/fake_bin/npx model_refused payload as CONFIGURATION_REFUSAL, paired 400/invalid_request_error bad-param and context-limit fixtures as REQUEST_REFUSAL, and a second provider wording. Single-shot adapter fixtures for openai chat/responses, anthropic and google proving the record is written from inside the except block, not only loop tests. Primary-refused-then-fallback-succeeds and intermediate-fallback-refused-then-later-success, both asserting the refused exact identity is excluded from a LATER routing decision with its trigger reason — the recurring P1. Fallback-already-quarantined is skipped, not retried. Unverified converted to unavailable by a refusal. DEV reroute to a remaining model; empty pool after a refusal produces the routing stop. Decomposition-assessment and escalation-advisor refusals. Reviewer/plan-review quarantine writes nothing to provider_health, capability history or reviewer failure counts. Unattributed refusal retried within the bounded budget and never quarantined. A landing merge-conflict-resolver dispatch against a quarantined model refuses at zero cost and returns the routing-stop text through _merge_branch without raising. Re-exec generation boundary: records written in generation 1 are observed by an inherited story in generation 2; a fresh sprint id starts clean.

criteria_mapping.criterion: A dispatch refused because the account may not call the selected model is classified as a configuration refusal, distinct from a request-level or transient failure. The classification does not depend on matching one provider's message text: a refusal the classifier cannot attribute is treated as transient and retried within the existing bounded retry budget, never quarantined and never retried unboundedly.

A configuration refusal quarantines that model for the remainder of the run. No later story, phase or role in that run routes to it, and every exclusion it causes is recorded in the routing decision with a reason naming the refusal that triggered it.
Quarantine applies to an unverified model as much as to one the availability answer called available: the refusal converts unverified to unavailable for the rest of that run.
A configuration refusal is a routing outcome, not an agent failure: it is never recorded against the model's capability history and never counts as a dev or review failure for the story.

The story whose dispatch was refused continues on the remaining models where any remain, and stops before further spend, naming the excluded models, where none do — the same outcome #2950 defines for an empty pool.
Quarantine is scoped to the run. The next run resolves availability afresh (#2949) rather than inheriting a quarantine that may no longer hold.

risks.description: An installed process-level registry is global mutable state, which can leak between tests or between two sprints in one process.
risks.mitigation: Copy rate_registry's shape exactly: install() plus a contextmanager scope that restores the prior value, and a lock for the concurrent sprint workers. Tests install their own scope; a second sprint in one process installs a fresh one, which is also what makes fresh-run isolation testable.

risks.description: Recording the refusal inside the adapter except blocks means the classifier runs on a partially-constructed provider exception and could mis-attribute.
risks.mitigation: The classifier requires both the structured pre-generation gate and the message rule, and defaults to UNATTRIBUTED_REFUSAL — bounded retry, no quarantine — on anything it cannot attribute. Over-classification, not under-classification, is the failure that costs an operator a usable model.

risks.description: Leaving the landing path unchanged means a no-model refusal there surfaces as a merge failure message rather than a first-class routing-stop status.
risks.mitigation: Deliberate and stated. The pre-dispatch refusal guarantees zero spend and the message carries the #2950 routing-stop text naming the excluded models, which is what the criterion asks for. Changing _resolve_merge_conflicts's bool, _merge_branch, land_story and its three callers to carry a status the operator reads as text anyway was rejected twice as disproportionate; if a later story needs a structured landing status, it is a separate change with its own justification.

risks.description: Sprint workers run concurrently, so a story already dispatched may still be using a model when another worker learns the quarantine.
risks.mitigation: The guarantee is scoped to later routing decisions and later dispatches. The lock ensures every subsequent selection and every subsequent run_agent pre-dispatch check observes the record.

risks.description: sprint-audit.yaml rehydration could resurrect a quarantine into what is genuinely a new run.
risks.mitigation: Gate rehydration on the same _previous_run_marker_present() + sprint_id pair the existing cost carry-forward at runner.py:683 already uses, so 'is this the same run continuing' is answered once, by one mechanism, for both spend and quarantine.
